To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the interferon regulatory factor 2 (IRF-2) protein serves as a constitutively active transactivator of HPV-16 transcription in keratinocytes, that HPV-16 E2 and E7 proteins downregulate IRF-2 expression and that HPV-16 transcriptional activation by IRF-2 is mediated by the IRF-1/2 family of transcription factors binding to an interferon response element in the HPV-16 early promoter.
the interferon regulatory factor (irf)-2 protein serves as an activator of the HPV16 major early promoter and that the irf-2 gene is negatively regulated by the HPV16 early gene, E7.
the interferon regulatory factors (1 and 2) are important in the establishment and maintenance HPV infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding the molecular basis for the persistence of human papillomavirus (HPV) infections, which is essential for development of effective vaccines against the virus and prevention of cervical cancer.
the molecular mechanisms of viral persistence and the development of novel therapies for cervical cancer.
the role of the interferon response in the regulation of early viral transcription.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IRF pathway is a key player during HPV persistence.
IRF-2 is an important mediator in the establishment of the HPV-IRF-2-E7 regulatory loop.
HPV-16 E2, IRF-2, and IRF-1 are all involved in the activation of the HPV- 16 early gene transcription.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HPV-16 genome has evolved to utilize the host interferon response pathway as a mechanism to regulate its own expression.
the HPV-16 early promoter is a target for both IRF-2 and IRF-1.
IRF-1/2 are critical mediators in the establishment and maintenance HPV persistence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HPV-16 E1 and E2 proteins, as well as the viral transforming genes, E6 and E7, are capable of activating the HPV-16 early promoter in a cell type-specific manner.
the HPV-16 early region is under the control of multiple transcriptional regulatory factors.
HPV-16 E2, E6 and E7 proteins are all involved in the regulation of the IRF-1, -2 and -7 pathways.
